objective: Assess whether the public Codex exchange window can be used as a reliable reference to a preserved collaboration episode and which claims the available material supports.

answer.usable_reference: Conditionally yes: an exact public commit and path identify the historical wrapper, whose independently acquired SHA-256 agrees with the attached check record. The window carries concrete archival message identifiers and an authored account of two changes in the continuation of work. It is useful as a source-bounded historical reference.
independently_verified: The supplied Medium view loads through the Opera connector and exposes links to raw content, a mutable public issue comment, and an immutable public wrapper revision.
The source wrapper acquired directly from raw.githubusercontent.com has SHA-256 40fa259a0ce7fd77485820d558af45354411b4c2863646db3cb2b83dfc8be64b, agreeing with the attached check-result.json.
The pinned renderer acquired directly has SHA-256 f336f897dcc2d62eadcf4492c9385df21c5c03b46aef2523486564b9310ecc86, agreeing with check-result.json.
Renderer lines 201-210 copy the body directory, read the wrapper as UTF-8 text, conditionally replace its data-medium-return field-prefix, and write the adapted text as UTF-8 bytes.
The pinned source wrapper and local HTTP wrapper are different. A deliberately simple literal prefix replacement on the raw decoded source did not reproduce the local wrapper.
source_based_content_observed: The public wrapper labels itself a preserved episode dated 4 October 2026 and explicitly says it does not show current agent activity.
Its embedded public record contains two Combat exchanges with explicit turn and message identifiers, Owner feedback, a First Hearth document pointer, and two authored before/after forks.
The first authored fork records a change from a transcript viewer to a window of concrete work-changing forks after the Combat response.
The second authored fork narrows continuity to activity during cognition/conversation within an active session, with life after closing or suspending the world outside the demonstrated claim.
The wrapper says the full trace also includes a third Feniks exchange; that linked full trace was not independently read in this trial.
reported_but_not_independently_repeated: The attached check-result.json reports all seven original-source hashes matching their recovery declarations and their local-preview copies.
The attached record reports fully reconstructed projection hash cba7f81b644c5b67d08d258c2d881cf20585c2d11e32612724e40a7cc935bfd6 matching its observed projection.
The embedded messages use exactTextVerified=true; I did not verify these texts against the original private conversations.
The Browser workpiece describes test-suite and recovery-metadata properties. The corresponding test file and recovery.json were not read.
unresolved: I did not independently reproduce the complete renderer transformation and compare it against current local bytes. My simple raw-text replacement omitted the read_text newline handling in the actual renderer.

The source9-source11 output was truncated by the command tool. The current local wrapper's independently computed SHA-256 and the first renderer acquisition metadata did not survive the returned output; they are not presented as independent confirmations.
I did not read or hash all seven recovered original files.

I did not independently authenticate the original conversations, prove full semantic fidelity, open the linked full third exchange, test window controls, or verify that the rewritten return navigation resolves.
The assessment is pinned to the revision offered by the entry view. I did not establish whether this is the newest public revision or inspect the local checkout branch/HEAD.
does_not_support: Live presence or currently continuing activity of the original agents.
A generalized controlled causal capability gain.
Authenticity of all original conversation texts merely from hash equality.
Universal byte preservation of wrappers through rendering.
answer.interpretation: Different wrapper bytes alone are not evidence of corruption. The renderer visibly transforms the wrapper, and its text read can normalize line endings. The complete byte correspondence remains a bounded unresolved check in this run.
